name: Pinus
provenance: Northern temperate softwood; resinous and fragrant when split.
tip: Softwood needs less force — a light swing often lands in the sweet band.

name: Quercus serrata
provenance: East Asian oak; dense rings and tough radial rays.
tip: Hard oak wants weight and a clean edge — under-swinging glances off.

name: Cryptomeria japonica
provenance: Japanese cedar (sugi); straight grain, aromatic heartwood.
tip: Follow the grain; sugi splits cleanly when force matches its softness.

name: Platanus
provenance: Plane / sycamore; interlocking grain can twist the wedge.
tip: Interlock fights the axe — precision matters more than raw power.

name: Eucalyptus globulus
provenance: Blue gum; dense eucalypt fiber, common plantation timber.
tip: Very hard — too light stalls; too heavy wastes energy and jars the handle.

name: Toona (Chinese cedar)
provenance: Chinese cedar / toon; warm reddish heartwood, medium soft.
tip: Medium hardness with a wide sweet zone — good for learning the slider.
